own_solution.law: Entropy is a state function: ΔS = mLf/T0 + mc ln(Tw/T0), using Lf = 334000 J/kg. Thus ΔS = 0.2[334000/273 + 4186 ln(313/273)].
assumptions: All ice present in the block when heating begins contributes to the target.
The stated constant liquid heat capacity applies through 313 K.
The water remains liquid and none evaporates, as stated.

T6035.regime: Tw < q; all listed boiling temperatures exceed the final temperature of 313 K.

T5693.regime: Tw < q; all listed boiling temperatures exceed the final temperature of 313 K.

notes: All certified numerical answers are correct within their displayed precision. For additional masses 0.07, 0.13 and 0.36 kg, the calculated answers are respectively 484.866263, 592.614321 and 1005.648545 J/K. Heater power cancels between power and heating duration. Earlier-run ice and dispenser ice have no dependency on the current block's entropy change. The stated numerical minimal pairs preserve their number and unit. I retract the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal defect: pass 2 explicitly identifies T4B97 and T3F4A as numeral-free controls and accurately describes their difference from their numerical twins; neither is claimed to be a number-preserving minimal pair. The outside-regime reference expression represents entropy accumulated up to the boiling temperature, rather than a complete solution beyond boiling; it is expressly excluded from the certified in-regime claim.
